players.product: RL10C liquid-hydrogen engines powering the Vulcan Centaur second stage

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 2026 revenue was $5.9 billion, up $455 million or 8% year-over-year, with all three segments contributing; segment operating income rose $79 million or 9% and segment operating margin was 16%, up 10 basis points (the prior-year quarter included a $92 million product line asset sale gain); GAAP EPS was $3.13, up 28%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 revenue $5.9 billion; +8% YoY; segment margin 16%; EPS $3.13

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 orders were $7.3 billion, a book-to-bill of 1.2 times (trailing 12-month book-to-bill 1.3 times); backlog increased by more than $1 billion to $42 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: orders $7.3 billion; book-to-bill 1.2 times; backlog $42 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Raised 2026 guidance (CFO): revenue $23.2 billion-$23.7 billion (both ends up $200 million), organic revenue growth 8%-10%; segment operating margin maintained at low 16%; diluted EPS $11.80-$12 (both ends up $0.40, after absorbing an approximate $0.20 headwind from the commercial space propulsion divestiture); free cash flow guidance of $3 billion reaffirmed. The revenue increase reflects stronger Space & Mission Systems performance and the AMDT3 constellation win, part of Golden Dome for America.
quarterly_data.figure: 2026 revenue $23.2 billion-$23.7 billion; EPS $11.80-$12; FCF $3 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: L3Harris was selected by the U.S. Space Force for the AMDT-3 satellite constellation and is the only company awarded all five contracts related to missile tracking; it sees a $9 billion space pipeline over the next several years across missile warning, missile defense and classified missions and has secured $2.4 billion in new contracts since the fourth quarter; operations on AMDT3 and classified satellite awards will ramp up in the rest of the year, and satellites will be replenished to keep the constellations operational.
quarterly_data.figure: $9 billion space pipeline; $2.4 billion new contracts since Q4

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Space & Mission Systems grew 7% to about $3 billion in Q2 (ISR, missionized aircraft, classified space, F-35 control systems, air traffic control modernization); segment margin 9.8%, down 60 basis points on a non-repeating $75 million prior-year product line sale gain, partly offset by better program performance and a $23 million net gain on segment investments; 2026 SMS revenue guidance raised $200 million to $11.7 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: SMS Q2 revenue +7% to about $3 billion; margin 9.8%; 2026 SMS revenue $11.7 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: in ISR L3Harris was awarded in Q2 the first phase of the next two U.S. Air Force electronic attack missionized business jets; internationally it has been awarded $3 billion of airborne early warning and control programs since the fourth quarter, with a $10 billion pipeline across the Middle East, Asia-Pacific and Europe.
quarterly_data.figure: $3 billion AEW&C awards since Q4; $10 billion pipeline

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Communications & Spectrum Dominance Q2 revenue was $1.9 billion, up 4% (international volume, electronic warfare, data links), with margin of 26.9%, up 230 basis points; 2026 segment margin raised to mid 25% from approximately 25%, with second-half revenue ramping on demand for smart software-defined radios and the VAMPIRE counter-UAS system. CEO: L3Harris will build on the NGC2 orders received in Q1 and Q2 and continue to bid and win in the second half; 'It's early on NGC2, our products resonate, and we are winning more than our fair share'.

CEO: L3Harris will execute its newly awarded $4 billion FAA contract, which could run through 2046 if options are exercised, leading a nationwide effort to rebuild and modernize the FAA's telecommunications infrastructure backbone connecting every tower, radar facility and air traffic control center, including modernizing more than 700 ground stations.
quarterly_data.figure: $4 billion FAA contract; through 2046 with options; more than 700 ground stations

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: L3Harris targets $500 million of new international VAMPIRE counter-UAS orders, building on a Q2 U.S. Army $100 million contract award; its Wraith Shield counter-UAS jamming software runs on its smart software-defined radios and the CEO expects it to contribute to licensing revenue in the years ahead.
quarterly_data.figure: $500 million VAMPIRE order target; $100 million U.S. Army contract

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Missile Solutions revenue grew 14% year-over-year in Q2 (16% in the business being retained, partly offset by lower growth in the commercial space propulsion business being divested), with segment margin substantially similar to the prior year. CFO expects missile business growth in the high teens over the next couple of years at a minimum and the propulsion business to grow 20%+; CEO: the ramp 'will probably take a couple of years' before the real significant spike in profitability and revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: Missile Solutions Q2 revenue +14% (16% retained business)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: shortly after quarter end L3Harris signed a framework agreement for seven years of THAAD and PAC-3 production, representing approximately $12 billion of future production revenue and $2 billion of future profit. It is making progress to nearly triple PAC-3 production for solid rocket motors, Attitude Control Motors and Lethality Enhancers; as the only company producing these PAC-3 solid rocket motors at scale today (with sole-source positions on Attitude Control Motors and Lethality Enhancers), it sees an opportunity to deliver solid rocket motor quantities above the 80% framework agreement. CEO: a 15%, 17%, 18% margin range is 'something to strive for' on the seven-year work.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately $12 billion of future production revenue; $2 billion of future profit; seven years

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: 'We are working with Lockheed to quadruple THAAD production, delivering all solid rocket motors and Divert and Attitude Control Systems for this program.'
quarterly_data.counterparty_role: THAAD production partner (L3Harris delivers solid rocket motors and Divert and Attitude Control Systems)

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: L3Harris is negotiating more than $20 billion in new missile contracts, potentially tripling its backlog. Since the Aerojet acquisition three years ago it increased R&D and capex in the business by a factor of 10, deliveries are up over 60% with substantially all delinquent deliveries eliminated, and operational efficiency improved 22%; the Department of War investment led it to accelerate its investment plans by 12-18 months.
quarterly_data.figure: more than $20 billion in negotiation; deliveries up over 60%; efficiency +22%

quarterly_data.signal: CEO/CFO: L3Harris is expanding missile production capacity by almost 1 million sq ft and building about 60 buildings for missiles; total missile capacity investments including finance lease activities were $136 million in Q2, and commitments for missile capacity (facilities, equipment, supply chain) total $2 billion; capex and R&D investment rose over 20% in the quarter. The new automated PAC-3 facility is expected online in late 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: almost 1 million sq ft; $136 million Q2 missile capacity investment; $2 billion commitments; PAC-3 facility late 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the new highly automated GMLRS factory (the Arsenal of Freedom building, with robotics, automated mixing, casting, curing and X-ray inspection cells with AI overlaid) comes online the month after the call and will more than double GMLRS capacity while reducing manufacturing times by 50%.
quarterly_data.figure: more than double capacity; manufacturing times reduced by 50%

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: L3Harris expects to close the sale of a majority interest in its commercial space propulsion business in August, after which it is no longer consolidated; the business generated revenue of $571 million and segment profit of $82 million in 2025, and revenue of $312 million and segment profit of $57 million Q2 year-to-date 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: 2025 revenue $571 million, segment profit $82 million; Q2 YTD 2026 revenue $312 million, segment profit $57 million

quarterly_data.signal: CFO: Q2 operating cash flow was $879 million and free cash flow $771 million; year-to-date free cash flow is $584 million, $124 million ahead of the prior year. International sales rose $254 million, up over 20%; the international sales mix increased by about 250 basis points in the last year or so to 23% of total revenue.
quarterly_data.figure: OCF $879 million; FCF $771 million; international 23% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: L3Harris is developing Red Wolf, a low-cost modular cruise missile, with the United States Marine Corps for precision strike, and says it is well positioned in the emerging low-cost interceptor market with proven propulsion and in-house seekers.

CEO: he expects debate on Department of War budgets but, with the country on a wartime footing, expects the highest defense budget in U.S. history and a supplemental budget to fund multi-year munition contracts; irrespective of where the budget ends up, L3Harris's outlook is positive.
